posts.author: lurkin
posts.content_md:
Hi all... I've come here hoping to finally be put out of my misery! I've searched the internet for around 6 months trying to get an answer so hope you guys may be the answer to my prayers! (I'm assuming if you don't know, no'one will!)

I work as an illustrator and have wanted for several years to have a hologram as the image on my business cards instead of the traditional kind. As far as I can find no'one offers this service... am I wrong?

To give a bit of background, the image wouldn't have to be my artwork as such so the hologram could be produced at the premises or I could supply all they needed, unless specialist equipment is used with the image.

The writing (ie, name, contact details etc) wouldn't have to be a part of the hologram, it could be printed either across the hologram or on the back of the card itself. As far as the hologram goes (you'll have to bare with me here!!!) it would be the traditional style(?) ie. not lenticular(?) like the ones I used to collect out of packets of cereal when I was young and like One I saw on the web of the queens portrait (although obviously that wouldn't be the image!!!)...

Well, I'm talking rubbish now, but does anyone know of anyone able/willing to do that?? Or would it just be too cost prohibative???

Thanks to anyone with any clue at all... and if you manage to work out what sort of hologram I want from my description I already take my hat off to you!

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
As with just about anything, it all depends on how much you can afford to spend.

A rainbow-style (IE, similar to what you see with wrapping paper) hologram card could probably be produced pretty "cheaply". It would be more expensive than typical business cards but you'd probably just be talking about a transparent rainbow layer on top of a normal business card. I don't know anyone who does this so it would probably be a custom job.

maybe your could combine a product like this...

[3M™ Transparent Hologram Security Laminate](http://products3.3m.com/catalog/ww/en001/security/-/node_GSXQ37GBCWbe/root_GST1T4S9TCgv/vroot_67FS85WMRKge/gvel_Z82KWJMW9Bgl/theme_ww_securitymarket_3_0/command_LongDescOutlinkHandler/output_html)

with inkjet card sheets you can print yourself. If you can get a 8.5" x 11" overlay sheet you could easily print your own cards, laminate the hologram sheet on top and use a paper cutter to cut the cards to size.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
If you want a true 3d image and not just color gratings on you business card then you will want the embossed hologram. Although these holograms can cost pennies if 100's of thousands are made they can be quite expensive for 500 or 1000 due to all the preliminary steps needed (artwork, master hologram, copy hologram, silverizing, nickel plating and finally the embossing process).

But for a really cool holographic business card that you can do yourself do the following;

Get some self adhesive holographic sheets (a google search for self adhesive holographic sheet will yield a large selection, I tried it with google images and found quite a bit).

Attach a piece of this sheet to some card stock the size a laser printer will handle.

Trim to card stock size.

Work out your lettering for business card on computer.

Print out on holographic side with laser printer.

Cut to business card size.

I have done this and a laser printer will print on the hologrphic sheet holographic side. You will have a holographic business card with lettering on the holographic side for a very inexpensive amount. Very eye catching.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: For around $3K you can get 1000 cards with custom embossed holograms. There are many suppliers although I have not used any lately. PM me and I can give you some leads.

posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
Hi Lurkin

A business I am involved in specialises in Hot Foil Printing. Amongst the many different types of foil available are some VERY eyecatching holographic foils. If used in the correct manner, that is to create an emphasis on certain aspects of the card, they can be very effective. As a designer i'm sure you will know exactly what I mean.

May I suggest that you find a local Hot Foil Printer and ask to see some samples of their work. You may be able to acheive the effect you require without going to huge expense. Hot Foiling is very underrated and is quite often overlooked by graphic designers, it can however acheive stunning results.

Cheers

Jem

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
> **Colin Kaminski:** For around $3K you can get 1000 cards with custom embossed holograms. There are many suppliers although I have not used any lately.

I may be mistaken, but custom embossed holography with 3D models is pretty much a thing of the past in this country. I never see them anymore in stores. There are probably still some companies that will produce them, but the demand must be very low indeed. (I'm only talking about embossed holograms made from sculptural objects, which is what I assume most people have in mind.) In other countries it may be a completely different story, in China or India for example. One person I know who has done resist masters continuously for many years told me that "it's a gimmick that's run it's course." I assume that's why "Holography Marketplace" isn't published anymore.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: The lab I have used in Hong Kong will work from Illustrator Artwork or models. I know there are still US people that will make a resist of anything you can afford. But for small run embossing I have only found overseas people.
